title: Metric Thermometer and Trace Budgeting Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a lightweight "metric thermometer" prioritization model and an associated trace-budgeting approach for inference-specific telemetry. Goal: give product and infra teams a practical, repeatable way to decide which metrics are live on operator dashboards, how many traces we should budget for them, and how to evolve the surface over time without exploding query cost.

Scope:
- Primarily for tokenized inference services (hosted API, Dedicated pools).
- Applies to metrics that feed dashboards, alerts, and causal investigations (latency, error, cache, routing, cost).
- Not a replacement for the metric contract template; this is a lightweight operational prioritization + sampling policy.

Why we need a thermometer:
We keep adding panels and trace anchors and the query/trace cost grows linearly while operator attention is limited. The thermometer gives a visual/operational cue (Core / Warm / Cold / Archive) with explicit signal obligations and trace budgets per metric class. This lets teams prune aggressively and set predictable trace consumption.

Metric Thermometer Levels (short):
- Core (aka "red"): top 8–12 signals per product surface. Must have: clear owner, SLA mapping, alerting thresholds, trace anchors for P90+ outliers. Query budget: high-priority probe (real-time) + 1000 traces/day budgeted for correlated investigation.
- Warm ("amber"): useful for runbook investigations and rollouts. Owned, have a clear derivation, no noisy alerts. Query budget: periodic probes + 100–500 traces/day.
- Cold ("teal"): diagnostic or experimental signals; collected at low resolution or sample-rate; no immediate alerting. Query budget: 10–50 traces/day.
- Archive ("blue"): historical/backfill-only metrics or heavy aggregations; access by request. No trace budget.

Example mapping for inference surface:
- request.latency.p50/p90/p99 => Core (traces anchored on > p95 requests)
- kv_cache.hit_rate => Core (small trace anchor on misses; probe showing heatmap by tenant)
- batching.mean_batch_size => Warm (correlate with latency; sample 1/200)
- model.fallback.rate => Core (trace every fallback up to budget; high signal for rollout gating)
- token_cost.per_request => Warm (cost dashboards; traces on top 1% cost requests)

Trace Budgeting Strategy (principles):
1) Fixed per-metric-class caps: allocate a per-day budget rather than unlimited sampling. Helps ops predict DB/zipkin/e2e cost.
2) Severity-weighted sampling: use higher probability for anomalous events (out-of-bound latency, error spikes, fallback events).
3) Session-anchored grouping: capture full session for sampled traces to preserve causality; count session once against budget.
4) Prefer span-preserving mini-traces for inexpensive root cause (e.g., KV miss + model load) when full trace exceeds budget.
5) Decay and reclaim: budgets are re-evaluated quarterly; unused budget can be reallocated to experiments.

Sampling Tiers (practical):
- Tier A (Core anchors): sample rate 1.0 for failures and p99+; otherwise 5% for p90–p99, 0.1% baseline.
- Tier B (Warm): sample 1% for anomalous slices, 0.05% baseline.
- Tier C (Cold): static low-rate 0.01% or on-demand.

Dashboard design notes (cost-aware panels):
- Single-panel-per-operator-rule: group metrics by function (latency/cost/cache) and show top-n tenant breakdowns only for Core signals.
- Heatmap widget: render the thermostat (Core/Warm/Cold) per-metric plus an estimated daily query cost in $ or tokens so product managers can see pivot cost.
- Microdash + deep-dive link: keep a small microdash (top 6 panels) for oncall and a second investigative dashboard with heavier queries and trace links accessible via a gated link.
- Quantify widget cost: add a tiny caption under each heavy panel with last-7-day query count and average cost estimate.

Runbook snippets (investigation prioritization):
- Step 1: Check Core thermometers and P95/P99 latency panel. If Core metrics are clean, move to Warm signals.
- Step 2: If Core flags a tenant spike, cross-reference kv_cache miss heatmap -> if misses high, sample KV-miss traces (within budget).
- Step 3: If traces indicate model-loading stalls, route to infra team and open JIRA with trace id and tenant.

Instrumentation checklist for adding a metric:
- Define owner and SLA mapping (who will respond?): add to metric contract.
- Thermometer level proposal (email/PR): include approximate query cost and trace budget.
- Implementation: ensure metric has a stable name, units, tags (tenant_id, model, region), and a sensible cardinality cap.
- Dashboard PR: propose a microdash slot or investigative slot; annotate cost.
- Release: wait 1 week, then measure utility; if < 1 investigation/month, consider moving down 1 level.

Migration plan (for heavy dashboards):
1) Audit current panels: run the 'panel-cost-extract' script (referenced in linked_artifacts).
2) Tag panels with preliminary thermometer level and owner.
3) Run a two-week sampling window with trace budgets applied.
4) Prune/compact: remove Cold panels or move them to the archive dashboard.

Open questions / proposals:
- Should we centralize trace budget enforcement in the control plane or leave it to each service? (Pros/cons discussion in #observability-budget slack thread).
- Define a simple billing metric for query-cost to show PMs (tokens billed vs operator queries).
- Can we implement a low-cost mini-trace format (span-minified JSON) for KV and model-load spans to reduce storage cost? (Draft PR linked).

Immediate action items:
- [ ] Owner alignment: Maya to run a 30-min sync with owners listed in the audit (by 2025-03-05).
- [ ] Add thermometer annotations to top-30 panels (Ravi + Sofia, target 2025-03-19).
- [ ] Implement per-metric daily trace cap enforcement prototype (ticket JIRA-OBS-4123).

Notes & references:
- Related: telemetry-cost playbook, trace-sampling-budget notes (see linked_artifacts).
- Historical context: this borrows from the "dashboard-tiering" proposals and the sampling experiments in Q4 2024.

If you're reviewing: please comment inline with suggested thermometer level and approximate monthly query cost for panels you own.
